title: Genesis Capital Allocation transfers are authorized to skip the Governance Poll and go straight to an Executive Vote
content:
Sky's normal path for a capital movement is Governance Poll first, then Executive Vote. Every Genesis Capital Allocation in this chunk suspends the first step with an identical clause: "This action is authorized to proceed directly to an Executive Vote without a prior Governance Poll." It appears for Keel (A.2.8.2.3.2.3), Obex (A.2.8.2.4.2.1.2.1), Osero (A.2.8.2.6.2.2.2.2), Skybase (A.2.8.2.7.2.2.2.1 and .2.2), Amatsu (A.2.8.2.8.2.1) and Ozone (A.2.8.2.9.2.1).

The rationale is implicit but consistent: the Accord itself was ratified through an Atlas Edit, so the substantive decision — whether to capitalize this counterparty at this size — has already been taken by governance. Re-polling it would only re-litigate a settled commitment, and a failed poll would put Sky in breach of an agreement it already signed.

The tradeoff is that the poll stage is where sentiment can still change cheaply. Once the authorization is written into the Atlas, the only remaining veto is the Executive Vote, which is a coarser instrument bundling many actions at once. The pattern therefore front-loads all deliberation to the moment the Accord text is edited into the Atlas — that edit, not the transfer, is the real decision point, and reviewers who treat Accord text as descriptive record rather than binding authorization will miss where the money was committed.
description: Recurs verbatim across Accords for Keel, Obex, Osero, Skybase, Amatsu and Ozone: signing the Accord is treated as the governance decision, leaving the Executive Vote as pure execution.
